terms.heading: Terms
terms.unavailable: The contract terms are unavailable right now.

staking.title: Deposits
staking.yieldRateNote: Simple, not compounding — yield never folds back into the earning base, so what you earn is a function of your deposit and time and nothing else.
staking.withdrawalsNote: Deposits are not locked. A withdrawal is limited only by what your debt allows: enough has to stay to keep your loan health above the liquidation line.

borrowing.title: Borrowing
borrowing.maxLtvNote: Your borrow limit, as a share of your deposit. A borrow that would cross it is refused rather than allowed and then liquidated.
borrowing.thresholdNote: Where loan health reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible.
borrowing.thresholdNoteGap: Where loan health reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible. The gap above your borrow limit is deliberate: it is the room a loan has to accrue interest before anyone can touch it.
borrowing.kinkNote: Where the borrow rate stops rising gently and starts rising steeply, so lenders are paid to refill a pool that is running dry.

liquidated.title: If you are liquidated
liquidated.closeFactorNote: The most of your debt one liquidation may clear. It caps what a single price dip costs you — the rest of your deposit survives it.
liquidated.bonusNote: The discount a liquidator takes on the collateral they seize, paid out of your deposit. It is what makes anyone show up to close an underwater loan, which is what keeps the pool solvent.
liquidated.fullNote: Below this loan health the close-factor cap is lifted and the whole loan may be cleared at once. It is derived on chain from the liquidation line and the bonus, not configured — it is precisely the point where a capped liquidation stops making a loan healthier.

rounds.title: Backing a side
rounds.intro: Odds come from how the pool splits, so the protocol never takes the other side of your view.
rounds.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement, so it is already inside the odds you were shown rather than deducted from a win afterwards.
rounds.entryCutoffNote: Entry closes before the round locks so nobody can back a side in the last second against a price they can already see moving.
rounds.minimumPerSideNote: A round whose losing side never reaches this is voided and every position is refunded in full — a one-sided pool has nothing to pay a winner from.

fees.heading: Protocol earnings
fees.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement. A voided round takes none at all — rake is only recorded on the resolve path — so a market on a slow feed earns nothing while it is voiding.
fees.rakeBound: Capped by the rake collected, not by the token balance, so this cannot reach money still owed to users — including a resolved round's unclaimed winnings.
fees.reservesNote: The protocol's cut of borrower interest, credited when interest accrues into the index rather than when a borrower pays.
fees.reservesBound: Subordinated to suppliers: a withdrawal is refused unless the pool still holds enough cash to meet every supplier claim afterwards. Credited interest that nobody has paid is not withdrawable.
fees.predatesTreasury: This contract was deployed before the stored treasury and has no treasury(). Its withdrawal still takes a destination, so it can only be called from a terminal — that is the state GHO-40 is about, and it clears on the next deploy.
fees.overAccrued: More than has accrued. The contract would refuse this.

stake.subtitle: Earns while it sits, and secures everything you borrow
stake.needsWallet: Your deposit, what it earns, and what you can borrow against it all live at your address.
stake.notConfigured: No deposit vault is configured for this network.

stake.partialExitBlocked: You have debt open against this deposit, so it can only be withdrawn in full. The loan is repaid from the proceeds and the rest comes back to you.
stake.neverLeaves: Your deposit never leaves to secure a loan — borrowing puts a claim on it and the money comes from the lending pool. It keeps earning the whole time, which is the point: you back your call without unwinding your deposit.

borrow.title: Borrow
borrow.subtitle: Borrow against your deposit, or repay what you owe
borrow.needsWallet: Your borrow limit comes from what you have deposited.
borrow.notConfigured: No vault is configured for this network.
borrow.overDebt: More than you owe. Repaying is capped at the debt.
borrow.interestNote: Interest accrues every second at the pool’s current rate, so the debt grows on its own between transactions. Borrowing stops at your borrow limit, which sits well below the liquidation line.

lend.title: Lend
lend.subtitle: Supply the pool that borrowers draw from, and earn what they pay
lend.notConfigured: No lending pool is configured for this network.
lend.unreadableDetail: The RPC call failed. Any balance you have supplied is unchanged — this screen just cannot see it right now.

warnings.exit-blocked: Every token in the pool is out on loan, so nothing can be withdrawn right now. Your balance keeps earning, and liquidity returns as borrowers repay.
warnings.exit-limited: More of your balance is out on loan than the pool holds in cash, so only part of it can be withdrawn right now. The rest returns as borrowers repay.
warnings.past-kink: The pool is lent out past its target, which is why the rate is high. The same fact makes exiting harder: the rate is steep here to pull supply in and slow borrowing down.

lend.connectToSupplyDetail: The pool figures above are the same for everyone. A supply balance is per address.

pool.heading: The lending pool
pool.borrowersPay: borrowers pay , and that is where the supply rate comes from
pool.utilizationNote: Utilization is the fraction of the pool that is out on loan. It is what you earn — idle liquidity pays nobody — and it is what stands between you and the exit, because money that is lent out is not money you can withdraw. The two readings are the whole decision.

lend.overLiquidity: More than the pool holds in cash. {amount} {symbol} is available right now — the rest of your balance is out as someone else’s loan and comes back as borrowers repay.
lend.supplyNote: Supplying lowers utilization, and with it the rate you are about to earn — the curve prices scarcity, so adding liquidity makes it less scarce. The figure above is the rate's input after your deposit lands.
lend.withdrawNote: Withdrawing raises utilization for everyone left in the pool, which raises the borrow rate and the supply rate together. Past the target the curve turns steep on purpose.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: Your deposit earns. Borrow against it. Back your call.

landing.headline: Back your call without unwinding your deposit.
landing.lede: Most ways of backing an opinion make you sell something first. Here your deposit stays put and keeps earning, and the position is funded by borrowing against it.
landing.readOnly: Nothing here needs a wallet to read. Connecting is read-only — no transaction is proposed.

stake.title: Deposit
stake.body: Deposit into the vault. It earns from the moment it lands, and it does not stop earning for anything that follows.

borrow.title: Borrow against it
borrow.body: Draw against the deposit rather than withdrawing it. What you borrow is secured by it, so the deposit never leaves and never stops working.

view.title: Back your call
view.body: Back a side of a market. Odds come from how the pool splits, so the protocol never takes the other side of your position.

risks.heading: What happens when it goes against you
risks.debtStands: <lead>A losing round does not clear the debt.</lead> The position was funded by a loan, and the loan stands whether the call was right or wrong. It is repaid from your deposit.
risks.interest: <lead>Interest accrues every second.</lead> A loan left open moves your loan health down on its own, with no price needing to move.
risks.liquidation: <lead>Below a loan health of 1.00 anyone may liquidate you.</lead> That is what keeps the pool solvent, and it is paid out of your deposit.
risks.liquidationBonus: <lead>Below a loan health of 1.00 anyone may liquidate you and take {bonus} of the collateral they seize.</lead> That is what keeps the pool solvent, and it is paid out of your deposit.
risks.voided: <lead>A round can be voided.</lead> If one side never fills, or the price feed cannot be read at settlement, the round refunds everybody in full rather than picking a winner.

landing.testnet: Testnet. The asset is a mock token you can mint for free, and every rule above is enforced on chain — the exact figures are on the overview once you connect.

resolve.explain: Resolving names the feed round at the close. Permissionless — anyone may send it.
resolve.notPublished: The feed has not published since this round closed. Nothing can settle it yet — that is the pinning rule doing its job, not a fault.
resolve.unreadable: The feed could not be read. Try again.
resolve.refused: Feed round {round} is the last one before the close, but the adapter will not read it — stale, or the sequencer was down, or the feed is paused. Resolving now would revert.
resolve.found: Feed round settles this at . The adapter accepted it on a dry run, so the transaction will land.
resolve.behindLock: That round predates the strike read, which the contract refuses. Something is wrong with the feed rather than with this round.

demo.heading: Publish a price
demo.explain: This market’s price is whatever you publish here. Settling a round takes <lead>two pushes</lead>: one before the close, which becomes the settlement price, and one after it, which proves the first was the last.
demo.badPrice: A price, with at most 8 decimal places — the feed’s scale.
demo.notOwner: Only {owner} can publish on this feed. Without that key the demo market cannot be settled at all.
